sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** — Guidelines and non-justiciable principles for framing laws by the government.
Enshrined in the **Constitution of India** on **26 January 1950**; drafted between **1946 and 1949**.
Contained in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution, covering **Article 36 to Article 51**.
Inspired by the **Irish Constitution of 1937**, which itself borrowed it from the **Spanish Constitution of 1931**.
Aims to establish a **Welfare State** (कल्याणकारी राज्य) in India, ensuring social, economic, and political justice.
**Non-justiciable** (cannot be enforced in courts), dynamic in nature, and acts as a moral obligation on the state.
High-yield static GK topic; questions frequently asked on **Article 40 (Panchayats)**, **Article 44 (UCC)**, and **Article 45**.
Described by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** as 'Novel Features' of the Indian Constitution; classified into Gandhian, Socialist, and Liberal-Intellectual ideologies.

items.title: Introduction and Part IV Framework
items.content:
• Covered under **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution from **Article 36 to Article 51**.
• Borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** (1937).
• **Article 36** defines the term **'State'** same as in Part III (Fundamental Rights).
• **Article 37** explicitly states that DPSP are **non-justiciable** (cannot be enforced by any court) but are **fundamental in the governance** of the country.

items.title: Classification of DPSP Ideologies
items.content:
• **Socialistic Principles:** Aim at social and economic equality (**Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A, 47**).
• **Gandhian Principles:** Based on Mahatma Gandhi's reconstruction programme (**Articles 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47, 48**).
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles:** Represent the ideology of liberalism (**Articles 44, 45, 48, 48A, 49, 50, 51**).

items.title: Mnemonic 1: Important Articles Sequence
items.content:
• **Mnemonic Phrase:** 'PAN-UN-CIV-CHILD-COW'
• **PAN:** **Article 40** (Panchayat organization)
• **UN:** **Article 44** (Uniform Civil Code)
• **CIV:** **Article 45** (Childhood care and education)
• **CHILD:** **Article 48** (Cow slaughter prohibition & agriculture)
• **COW:** **Article 50** (Separation of Judiciary from Executive)

items.title: Socialist Principles Deep Dive
items.content:
• **Article 38:** Promote welfare of people by securing a **social order** based on justice.
• **Article 39:** Certain principles of policy to be followed by the state, including **equal pay for equal work** for men and women.
• **Article 39A:** Free legal aid to the poor (**Added by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976**).
• **Article 41:** Right to work, to education, and to public assistance in certain cases.

items.title: Gandhian & Liberal Principles
items.content:
• **Article 40:** Organization of **Village Panchayats**.
• **Article 44:** Uniform Civil Code (**UCC**) throughout the territory of India.
• **Article 48A:** Protection and improvement of **environment and wildlife** (**Added by 42nd Amendment, 1976**).
• **Article 51:** Promotion of **international peace and security**.

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Amendments Adding New DPSPs
items.content:
• **Mnemonic Phrase:** '42 & 44 Add Legal & Coop'
• **42nd Amendment (1976):** Added Articles **39(f)**, **39A**, **43A**, and **48A**.
• **44th Amendment (1978):** Added Article **38(2)** (minimizing inequalities in income).
• **97th Amendment (2011):** Added Article **43B** (Cooperative societies).

items.term: Trick 2: Article 40 vs Article 44 vs Article 48
items.definition: Notice the multiples of 4: **40** (Panchayat - local governance), **44** (Uniform Civil Code - uniform law), **48** (Agriculture/Cows - rural economy). All are crucial for UPSSSC PET.
Use the code **'ECL'**: **E**nvironment (Art 48A), **C**hildren/Legal Aid (Art 39A), **L**abour participation in management (Art 43A). All added in **1976**.
Associate **Part III (Fundamental Rights)** with **'COURT'** (Justiciable) and **Part IV (DPSP)** with **'CONSCIENCE'** (Non-justiciable moral duties of the state).
Think of **'50-50 Partnership'** between Judiciary and Executive being broken up — meaning **Separation of Judiciary from Executive**.
Associate **Article 51** with **'UN 51'** or **'World Peace'** — India's commitment to international security and Panchsheel principles.
Students often think DPSP can be enforced in High Courts or Supreme Court. **Correct fact:** DPSP is **non-justiciable** under Article 37; Fundamental Rights are justiciable under Article 32 and 226.

Students confuse Article 45 with Article 21A. **Correct fact:** Article 45 now covers **Early Childhood Care for children below 6 years**, while Article 21A covers **Free & Compulsory Education for ages 6 to 14** (inserted by 86th Amendment 2002).
Students mix up Fundamental Rights (USA) with DPSP (Ireland). **Correct fact:** DPSP is borrowed from **Ireland**, whereas Fundamental Rights are from the **USA**.
Students confuse Part III and Part IV. **Correct fact:** Part III is Fundamental Rights (Art 12-35), and **Part IV is DPSP (Art 36-51)**.
Thinking Ireland created DPSP. **Correct fact:** Ireland borrowed it from the **Spanish Constitution of 1931** before India borrowed it from Ireland.
Assuming DPSP has zero legal backing. **Correct fact:** While courts cannot enforce them, many laws like MGNREGA, Wildlife Protection Act, and Panchayati Raj Acts were enacted to give effect to DPSP.
DPSP is enshrined in **Part IV (Article 36-51)** of the Indian Constitution and is borrowed from **Ireland**.
The primary objective is to establish a **Welfare State** ensuring social and economic democracy.
Under **Article 37**, DPSP cannot be enforced in any court of law, but they are **fundamental in the governance** of the country.
Directs the state to organize **Village Panchayats** and endow them with necessary powers.
Enjoins the state to secure a **Uniform Civil Code** throughout the territory of India.
Organize agriculture on modern lines and prohibit slaughter of **cows, calves, and milch cattle**.
Protection and improvement of **environment, forests, and wildlife** (added by 42nd Amendment, 1976).
Take steps to **separate the judiciary from the executive** in the public services of the State.
Promote international peace, security, and maintain just and honorable relations between nations.
Key amendments adding new DPSPs include the **42nd Amendment (1976)**, **44th Amendment (1978)**, and **97th Amendment (2011)**.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize specific article numbers such as Article 40, Article 44, Article 45, and Article 48 as questions are directly asked matching articles with their subjects.
UPSSSC often sets traps by stating that DPSPs are enforceable by Supreme Court writs. Remember: **Only Fundamental Rights** (Part III) are enforceable via writs (Article 32), not DPSP.
Keep a clear distinction between Gandhian, Socialist, and Liberal-Intellectual categories of DPSP, as classification-based questions appear frequently in UP exams.
Do not confuse the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002). It modified Article 45 for early childhood care and simultaneously added Article 21A for Right to Education.

keyTakeaways: DPSP is contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) and borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
DPSP principles are **non-justiciable**, serving as moral and political guidelines for state policy.
**Article 40** deals with Village Panchayats, which is a key Gandhian principle.
**Article 44** advocates for a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) across India.
**Article 48A** and **Article 39A** were added via the landmark **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
The ultimate goal of DPSP is to create a socio-economic **Welfare State** in India.
